correctness.rationale: The section x trivializes the line orthogonal to E. The frame fibration U(2) -> U(3) -> S^5 has surjective boundary pi_5(S^5) -> pi_4(U(2)) because pi_4(U(3)) = 0. The image of the generator is the clutching class, hence is nonzero in Z/2. Here pi_4(U(2)) follows from the S^1 x SU(2) cover and pi_4(S^3) = Z/2; pi_4(U(3)) is stable and zero. The sphere quotients U(k+1)/U(k) = S^(2k+1) also give injectivity of rank-two stabilization through pi_3, ruling out the lower sphere dimensions. Each idempotent section has constant rank; rank one would split E into two trivial lines because H^2(S^5;Z)=0. A disconnected compact spectrum gives a nontrivial idempotent by holomorphic functional calculus. For m >= 2, clutching in the stable range trivializes E^{oplus m}, and the fiberwise endomorphism identification is a unital *-isomorphism on sections. A constant diagonal realizes 2m singleton components. For the upper bound, if a compact spectrum had more than 2m components, select 2m+1 points in distinct components; compact Hausdorff components are quasi-components, so finitely many clopen cuts followed by grouping give a clopen partition into 2m+1 nonempty parts. Its idempotents have positive constant ranks summing to 2m, a contradiction. This covers arbitrary spectra, not just finite ones. value.rationale: The useful witness is not merely non-invariance under Morita equivalence, which elementary commutative examples already show. It isolates a global bundle obstruction that suppresses all spectral splitting in an algebra with two-dimensional matrix fibers and disappears entirely in every full amplification. The exact rank bound and restricted first sphere dimension identify how sharply this obstruction can disappear in a natural noncommutative homogeneous example.
